source_type: own release (official USMLE sample test question booklets, usmle.org)
revision: booklet versions: Step 1 updated April 2026; Step 2 CK updated July 2023; Step 3 updated June 2026 (files served under /sites/default/files/2021-10/)
license: Copyright FSMB and NBME, all rights reserved; booklets marked "For Public Release"
split: all sample items (Step 1 119, Step 2 CK 120, Step 3 137)
text: subset (about 54 items sit on pages with figures and reference an image such as a photograph, radiograph or ECG; identifiable from the stem, list needs a manual check)
request_fields: vignette/question stem + lettered options (some stems include lab tables); answer key at end of each booklet
notes: Official URLs from usmle.org/exam-resources/step-1-materials/step-1-sample-test-questions, .../step-2-ck-materials/step-2-ck-sample-test-questions and usmle.org/prepare-your-exam/step-3-materials/step-3-sample-test-questions. Text is downloadable (text-layer PDFs; extracted with pdftotext). Item counts parsed from the booklets match their block tables. Image-item flag: items on PDF pages containing embedded images whose stem mentions a figure/photograph/x-ray etc. (Step 1 ~22, Step 2 CK ~19, Step 3 ~13). Booklets are revised over time, so the versions labs used may differ from these. Step 3 CCS cases are not included. Checked 2026-10-04; no LLMs or API keys used.

rendering.rule: multiple choice: the question stem (preceded by the shared abstract or vignette, then a blank line, for items in a set) then the options one per line as "A. ..." (source letters)
rendering.image_rule: exclude an item if its stem, shared stimulus or set notice matches any of: \b(photographs?|photomicrographs?|micrographs?|drawings?|diagrams?|figures?|illustrations?|images?|pedigree|plot|graphs?|curves|advertisement displayed)\b | \b(x-rays?|radiographs?|CT scans?|MRIs?|ECGs?|electrocardiograms?|tracings?|scans?|smears?|findings?|lesions?|rash|\w+graphy|\w+grams?)\b[^.;:]{0,80}?(\b(is|are)\s+shown\b|:\s*shown\b) | \b(findings?|lesions?|appearance)\s+(as\s+)?shown\b | \bas shown\b(?!\s+in\s+the\s+table) (case-insensitive); these refer to a picture (photograph, x-ray, ECG, drawing, pedigree, advertisement, plot) that is not in the text layer
